Sort values

Source: R/key-order.R
key_sort.Rd

key_sort() returns x sorted, as sort(x, method = "radix") does, by the order of key_order(). The result remembers that it is sorted and whether it holds a missing value, so a later sort(), is.unsorted() or anyNA() on it answers at once, without a pass over the values. Modifying the result in place forgets both.

Usage

key_sort(x, decreasing = FALSE, na.last = TRUE, collate = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A key vector: integer, double, logical, character, factor, integer64, Date, POSIXct, or a list of raw vectors.

decreasing

TRUE or FALSE.

na.last

TRUE, FALSE or NA; for key_rank() also "keep", which ranks a row with a missing key NA.

collate

FALSE sorts strings by bytes; TRUE in the order of the current locale, as stringi::stri_order() does. TRUE needs the stringi package, and is a zutable_collate_error without it.

Value

x in sorted order, with its class and levels; without its missing values when na.last = NA.

Details

Numbers, logicals, factors and dates are marked. Strings are not marked sorted, since base R's sortedness of strings is its own collation, which byte order and stringi's need not match, and base R reads no missing value mark on strings; nor is an integer64 vector, whose order is not that of its doubles.

Examples

s <- key_sort(c(3, 1, NA, 2))
s
#> [1]  1  2  3 NA
is.unsorted(s, na.rm = TRUE)
#> [1] FALSE
key_sort(c("b", "A", "a"))
#> [1] "A" "a" "b"
if (requireNamespace("stringi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  key_sort(c("b", "A", "a"), collate = TRUE)
}
#> [1] "a" "A" "b"
